title: Scarlet fever
stem: Paediatric area. Hoi-yan, 5, has had a sore throat and fever for 2 days, and today a rough red rash. Her mother wants to know what it is, whether she can go to school, and whether her baby brother is at risk. Examine and counsel.
notes:
Checked against the Hong Kong Centre for Health Protection (scarlet fever is a notifiable disease in HK), UKHSA guidance on scarlet fever and invasive group A streptococcus (2023), and NICE CKS.

Scarlet fever (Streptococcus pyogenes toxin): fever, sore throat, strawberry tongue, flushed cheeks with circumoral pallor, a fine sandpaper-like rash starting on the chest and spreading, accentuated in skin creases (Pastia's lines), later peeling of fingers and toes. Throat swab to confirm where available. Treatment: phenoxymethylpenicillin for 10 days (amoxicillin is an alternative; azithromycin/clarithromycin if penicillin-allergic). Exclude from school or nursery until 24 hours after starting antibiotics. Notify in HK (CHP). Complications: otitis, sinusitis, peritonsillar abscess; rarely rheumatic fever, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, invasive GAS (toxic shock, necrotising fasciitis) — safety-net for worsening. Contacts: hygiene; household contacts treated if symptomatic; heightened vigilance for invasive disease, especially with concurrent chickenpox.

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Face, tongue, throat, rash texture, skin creases, nodes, hydration.

Face.r: Flushed cheeks, pale around the mouth; red bumpy 'strawberry' tongue.
Face.mark: Finds strawberry tongue and circumoral pallor

Face.r: Enlarged red tonsils with exudate; tender anterior cervical nodes.

Skin.t: Feel the rash; look in the elbow creases
Skin.r: Fine rough 'sandpaper' rash on the trunk; red lines in the elbow creases.
Skin.mark: Identifies sandpaper rash and Pastia's lines

steps.label: Talk to her mother
steps.hint: Diagnosis, antibiotics 10 days, school exclusion 24 h, notification, siblings, warning signs.

opts.t: It's scarlet fever — a throat infection with streptococcus bacteria that makes a toxin, which causes the rash. It's treated easily with antibiotics.

turns.line: Antibiotics for how long? Can she go to school?

opts.t: Penicillin for the full 10 days, even when she feels better, to prevent complications. She can go back to school 24 hours after starting it. We report scarlet fever to the Department of Health.
opts.mark: Explains 10-day course, school exclusion and notification

opts.t: Three days of antibiotics; school tomorrow morning is fine.

Wash hands well, don't share cups or towels. If he gets a fever, sore throat or rash, bring him to be seen. Bring her back at once if she's getting worse, very sleepy, not drinking, or has a painful swollen limb or a rash that looks like a burn.
opts.mark: Advice for contacts and safety-netting for invasive GAS
